architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity

architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The established failure mode is formulation-dependent thermal-hold viscosity drift: local E5 drift is much larger than E1 drift, while E2 shows substantial realization variability. The declared intent is performance_mitigation, so both independently supported intervention axes must remain active; a single acrylic-only point would be only a mechanistic control. S1C41 is therefore selected as the lowest-burden full-coverage candidate, not because it is closest to an external literature percentage. Local experiments support the E2 reactive-core anchor, the distinction between thermal response and hold stability, and the need for state calibration. The paper-derived rheological rule supports using a 120 C one-point state anchor because realization state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a shared thermal-response shape remains transferable within the local chemistry family. Curated PUR literature/database priors support only the broad acrylic-like 15-20 wt% region and a minor tackifier-like region near 5 wt% and below about 10 wt%; they do not predict S1C41's wet-lab drift. The conservative design constraint is to preserve the E2 core, remain within 80-130 C and 15-90 minutes, use matched process history, and require full hold trajectories plus replicate repeatability. The Skeptic's objections are resolved by requiring matched remeasurement of E1 and E5, explicit replicate-level comparison, verified modifier functionality and recalculated NCO:OH balance, and a prespecified response to failed state calibration. The Robustness Adjudicator's objection is resolved by treating this as an uncertainty probe before interpreting the performance result; S1C46 and S1C51 remain escalation candidates rather than replacing the minimum-sufficient full-coverage test.

action_requests.reason: Required canonical bridge before candidate ranking. Use its formulation-only versus state-aware comparison, state-shift master curve, one-point calibration result, local temperature-sensitivity coordinate, and E1/E5 hold-drift contrast to decide whether state calibration, thermal response, or hold stability should dominate the experiment.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the measured low-drift reference trajectory and descriptors for direct comparison with candidate hold behavior; this is directly commensurate local evidence.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the measured high-drift reference trajectory and descriptors so the mitigation target is defined against the established local failure mode rather than against an external percentage.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: Quantify realization/process-state uncertainty around the original reactive-core anchor before treating nominal viscosity or temperature sensitivity as intrinsic material properties.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local objective is established, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 anchor, independent acrylic and tackifier axes, and historical/claim boundary before comparing candidate formulations.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Obtain source-level analogue evidence for chemically plausible acrylic intervention regions. Treat approximately 15 to 20 wt% as directional or analogue anchors and the 25 wt% low-OH comparison as comparative stability support, not as a local optimum.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Obtain source-level evidence for a bounded minor tackifier axis. Use the below-about-10 wt% guidance and modifier-family comparisons as conservative design bounds or directional evidence, not as exact formulation targets.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold SI over 15 to 60 minutes and 15 to 90 minutes at 120 C
Absolute viscosity drift trajectory rather than nominal viscosity alone
Viscosity level at anchor temperatures within 80 to 130 C
Temperature-response slope or local apparent temperature-sensitivity coordinate
Need for state calibration and sensitivity to realization/process state
Stoichiometric feasibility and preservation of the E2 reactive-core anchor
Acrylic-like modifier loading and evidence-supported modifier functionality or identity
Minor tackifier loading within the bounded 0 to 10 wt% region
Distance from directly measured composition and temperature support
External evidence directness: commensurate numeric anchor versus directional analogue versus conservative extrapolation control
counterfactual_checks: Would the candidate still be preferred if nominal viscosity were ignored and only hold drift plus repeatability were optimized?
Would the candidate remain preferred if state calibration were unavailable or showed substantial process-state dependence?
Does the proposed benefit persist relative to both the low-drift E1 reference and the high-drift E5 reference under matched hold conditions?
Is the predicted improvement attributable only to an external directional percentage rather than local measurements?
Would a single acrylic-only intervention be safer if the combination's tackifier contribution is not independently supported?
Would the conclusion change if the 15 to 20 wt% acrylic anchors were treated as noncommensurate analogues rather than numeric anchors?
Does the candidate remain inside measured temperature and time domains without relying on unsupported extrapolation?
Could the apparent improvement be explained by realization or process-state differences rather than composition?
Does the candidate satisfy stoichiometric and process constraints while preserving the original E2 reactive-core identity?
Is the planned measurement set capable of distinguishing viscosity level, thermal response, hold stability, and repeatability rather than collapsing them into one score?
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result candidate experiment point that mitigates thermal-hold viscosity drift while remaining inside measured temperature support and bounded, evidence-supported modifier regions.
design_implications: Use performance_mitigation rather than single-factor causal isolation because the failure mode is already established and the immediate objective is to reduce drift.

A multi-component intervention is admissible: an independently supported acrylic-like axis may be combined with a bounded minor tackifier-like axis, provided the reactive-core identity and stoichiometric/process constraints remain explicit.
Prefer candidate regions around approximately 15 to 20 wt% acrylic-like modifier, with 25 wt% treated as an upper evidence-supported stability probe rather than an assumed optimum.
Keep the tackifier-like modifier at a minor level within the available 0 to 10 wt% lattice and treat its evidence as directional.
Do not optimize only viscosity at one temperature; require a measured hold trajectory and temperature sweep.
Anchor comparisons within 80 to 130 C and within the measured 15 to 90 minute hold window.
Account explicitly for process history, realization state, and stoichiometric balance when comparing candidate formulations.
Do not use the held-out formulation identity or outcome, and do not infer exact composition recovery from the candidate lattice.
Preserve source units and treat external numeric values as commensurate only when temperature, metric, and formulation context are genuinely comparable.
material_regularities_to_use: The original E2 reactive-core anchor has monotonic viscosity decrease from 80 to 130 C, with descriptive Andrade fits having high R2 but substantial run spread.
E2 nominal repeatability is poor: CV is approximately 0.46 to 0.58 across 80 to 130 C, with max/min ratios approximately 2.8 to 3.6.
Thermal response and thermal-hold stability are distinct response dimensions and must not be conflated.
The E1/E5 original thermal-hold contrast establishes that hot-hold drift can differ strongly between formulations at 120 C over the measured 15 to 90 minute window.
The state-shift master-curve and one-point calibration findings must determine whether process or realization state calibration is required.
The next experiment should be judged on hold-stability improvement and repeatability as well as nominal viscosity level.
The measured temperature support is 80 to 130 C; extrapolation outside this range is not supported.
External acrylic anchors near 15 to 20 wt% and a 25 wt% low-OH acrylic stability comparison are directional or analogue evidence, not exact local optima.
External minor-tackifier anchors below about 10 wt% support a bounded secondary axis but do not establish its local effect.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold viscosity drift is the primary established failure mode, with E5 showing much larger SI drift than E1 at 120 C; high nominal run-to-run spread in E2 also makes a single viscosity value an unreliable sole objective. The causal molecular mechanism is not established by rheology alone.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep at 80, 90, 100, 110, 120, and 130 C, with preserved source units
Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 C over at least the measured 15, 30, 60, and 90 minute points
SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0 at 15 to 60 and 15 to 90 minutes
Initial and time-resolved viscosity values, not only endpoint SI
Replicate runs sufficient to estimate descriptive CV and max/min ratio
Recorded formulation composition, stoichiometric balance, preparation history, and thermal history
State calibration or equivalent realization-state record if the state-aware summary shows material state shifts
Comparison against the original E1 low-drift and E5 high-drift references under matched measurement conditions
uncertainty_triggers: State-aware modeling does not improve prediction or one-point state calibration is not reproducible
Candidate temperature response requires extrapolation outside 80 to 130 C
Candidate hold behavior is observed outside the 15 to 90 minute measured window
Run-to-run spread remains comparable to or larger than the apparent formulation effect
Stoichiometric balance or process history differs materially from the E2 anchor

robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 directly tests thermal-hold viscosity drift at 120 C over the established 15-90 minute failure window while preserving the E2 reactive-core proportions.

The Planner declares performance_mitigation, not causal_isolation. A dual-axis intervention is therefore appropriate, and S1C41 covers both independently supported acrylic_like and minor_tackifier_like axes.

S1C41 is a low-burden full-coverage candidate among the proposed primary points, so its rank is not based on burden alone. However, the tackifier evidence is directional and the 15 wt% acrylic level is noncommensurate lower-region evidence.
The recommendation remains defensible as an evidence-region test: it uses a supported acrylic region and a bounded minor tackifier level rather than relying on exact literature distance.

State-aware calibration, complete process-history recording, temperature sweeps, and matched holds are appropriate, but every candidate has substantial process-state uncertainty and one-point calibration must be demonstrated reproducible after modifier addition.

The proposed trajectory, SI15-60, SI15-90, temperature sweep, replicates, and E1/E5 comparisons can adjudicate mitigation, but the plan lacks prespecified replicate-level effect-size and repeatability rules.

E1 and E5 are single original runs from different operators, yet their SI values are used as fixed thresholds. They should be remeasured under the state-calibrated protocol or incorporated through an explicit uncertainty model.
Preservation of E2 stoichiometry cannot be assumed until AC1920 and TK100 functionality and reactive-group contributions are verified and the complete NCO:OH balance is recalculated.

The Skeptic identified serious adjudication gaps but not a reason to abandon the full-coverage performance strategy. The appropriate response is an uncertainty probe and protocol correction rather than a causal-isolation rerank.

counterfactual_failures: The proposal states that nominal viscosity should not dominate, but no explicit decision rule defines how S1C41 would be judged if hold drift improves while repeatability or viscosity level worsens.
The proposal does not specify how the conclusion changes if state calibration is unavailable or irreproducible, despite the large E2 realization spread and the state-aware model's importance.

The candidate remains a combined intervention even though no local result establishes that the tackifier axis contributes to drift mitigation; this is permissible for performance mitigation but limits mechanistic interpretation.

The rationale for preferring S1C41 over S1C46/S1C51 is consistent with minimum sufficient intervention, but no prespecified rule states when a larger full-coverage point would replace it after an inadequate result.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.

experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
